title: Offline support with a service worker
when: The user wants a site or app to open without a connection, or to cache its files for fast repeat visits.
prompt:
Goal: A versioned service worker that precaches the app shell, serves it offline, and updates without trapping users on old files.
Steps:
1. Register from main.js when "serviceWorker" in navigator: navigator.serviceWorker.register("./sw.js"); keep sw.js at the root so its scope covers the app.
2. Define const CACHE = "app-v1" and ASSETS as relative URLs: ./, ./index.html, ./style.css, ./main.js, icons.
3. install: event.waitUntil(caches.open(CACHE).then((c) => c.addAll(ASSETS))); activate: delete caches not named CACHE, then clients.claim().
4. fetch: handle only same origin GET; navigations go network first with the cached index.html as fallback; static files go cache first and store fresh copies.
5. Bump CACHE whenever an asset changes and tell the user when registration.waiting holds a new version.
Quality bar:
- After one visit the app opens with the network off.
- Navigations never end on a raw offline error page.
- Old caches are removed on activate.
Pitfalls:
- Caching POST or cross origin responses blindly.
- Absolute paths that break when the app lives in a subfolder.
- Testing over file://; service workers need localhost or HTTPS.
Verify:
- [ ] sw.js has install, activate and fetch listeners.
- [ ] Every ASSETS path exists.
- [ ] activate deletes old caches.
- [ ] Registration is feature detected.
Output: sw.js at the project root and the registration snippet in main.js.

examples.input: quero que meu app funcione sem internet
examples.output: sw.js precaching index.html, style.css, main.js under app-v1, network first navigations with cached fallback
